cues.zh: 这种令人沉浸其中的丑陋
cues.en: The immersive ugliness

cues.zh: 在美国我们日常环境中的这种丑陋
cues.en: of our everyday environments in America

cues.zh: 是熵变得可见了。
cues.en: is entropy made visible.

cues.zh: 我们无法高估我们所产生的绝望的程度
cues.en: We can't overestimate the amount of despair

cues.zh: 我们正在用这样的地方制造绝望。
cues.en: that we are generating with places like this.

cues.zh: 而主要是，我想说服大家，我们必须做得更好
cues.en: And mostly, I want to persuade you that we have to do better

cues.zh: 如果我们想在美国继续文明的事业。
cues.en: if we're going to continue the project of civilization in America.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这无济于事。
cues.en: By the way, this doesn't help.

cues.zh: 在这里，没有人因为那个而过得更好。
cues.en: Nobody's having a better day down here because of that.

cues.zh: 你可以用很多方式来描述这个。
cues.en: There are a lot of ways you can describe this.

cues.zh: 你知道，我喜欢称它为“全国汽车贫民窟”。
cues.en: You know, I like to call it "the national automobile slum."

cues.zh: 你可以称它为郊区蔓延。
cues.en: You can call it suburban sprawl.

cues.zh: 我认为把它称为
cues.en: I think it's appropriate to call it

cues.zh: 世界历史上最大的资源错配是恰当的。
cues.en: the greatest misallocation of resources in the history of the world.

cues.zh: 你可以称它为一团技术异化外部性的烂摊子。
cues.en: You can call it a technosis externality clusterfuck.

cues.zh: 这对我们来说是个巨大的问题。
cues.en: And it's a tremendous problem for us.

cues.zh: 对我们来说，最突出、最显著的问题在于
cues.en: The outstanding -- the salient problem about this for us

cues.zh: 这些是不值得关心的地方。
cues.en: is that these are places that are not worth caring about.

cues.zh: 我们还会再谈谈这一点。
cues.en: We're going to talk about that some more.

cues.zh: 场所感：
cues.en: A sense of place:

cues.zh: 你创造有意义、有品质、有特色之场所的能力
cues.en: your ability to create places that are meaningful and places of quality and character

cues.zh: 完全取决于你用建筑界定空间的能力，
cues.en: depends entirely on your ability to define space with buildings,

cues.zh: 以及运用建筑的词汇、语法、
cues.en: and to employ the vocabularies, grammars,

cues.zh: 句法、节奏和模式的能力
cues.en: syntaxes, rhythms and patterns of architecture

cues.zh: 来告诉我们自己是谁。
cues.en: in order to inform us who we are.

cues.zh: 美国的公共领域有两个角色：
cues.en: The public realm in America has two roles:

cues.zh: 它是我们文明和公民生活的栖居之所，
cues.en: it is the dwelling place of our civilization and our civic life,

cues.zh: 也是公共利益的物质体现。
cues.en: and it is the physical manifestation of the common good.

cues.zh: 而当你贬损公共领域时，
cues.en: And when you degrade the public realm,

cues.zh: 你自然会贬损公民生活的品质
cues.en: you will automatically degrade the quality of your civic life

cues.zh: 以及在那里发生的公共生活和社群生活一切活动的特色。
cues.en: and the character of all the enactments of your public life and communal life that take place there.

cues.zh: 在美国，公共空间主要以街道的形式存在
cues.en: The public realm comes mostly in the form of the street in America

cues.zh: 因为我们没有那些上千年历史的大教堂广场
cues.en: because we don't have the 1,000-year-old cathedral plazas

cues.zh: 和古老文化中的集市广场。
cues.en: and market squares of older cultures.

cues.zh: 而你界定空间、创造值得珍视之场所的能力
cues.en: And your ability to define space and to create places that are worth caring about

cues.zh: 全都源自我们称之为公民设计文化的一整套文化体系。
cues.en: all comes from a body of culture that we call the culture of civic design.

cues.zh: 这是一套知识、方法、技能和原则
cues.en: This is a body of knowledge, method, skill and principle

cues.zh: 却在二战后被我们扔进了垃圾堆
cues.en: that we threw in the garbage after World War II

cues.zh: 认定不再需要它了，不打算再用它了。
cues.en: and decided we don't need that anymore; we're not going to use it.

cues.zh: 结果，我们环顾四周就能看到后果。
cues.en: And consequently, we can see the result all around us.

cues.zh: 公共空间不仅要告诉我们身处地理上的何处，
cues.en: The public realm has to inform us not only where we are geographically,

cues.zh: 还要告诉我们身处文化中的何处。
cues.en: but it has to inform us where we are in our culture.

cues.zh: 我们从何而来，我们是怎样的人，而且它需要，
cues.en: Where we've come from, what kind of people we are, and it needs to,

cues.zh: 借此让我们瞥见我们将去向何方
cues.en: by doing that, it needs to afford us a glimpse to where we're going

cues.zh: 从而让我们安住于一个充满希望的当下。
cues.en: in order to allow us to dwell in a hopeful present.

cues.zh: 如果说有一件非常——
cues.en: And if there is one tremendous --

cues.zh: 如果说我们建造的地方有一个巨大的灾难，
cues.en: if there is one great catastrophe about the places that we've built,

cues.zh: 过去50年里我们为自己创造的人类环境，
cues.en: the human environments we've made for ourselves in the last 50 years,

cues.zh: 那就是它剥夺了我们活在充满希望的当下的能力。
cues.en: it is that it has deprived us of the ability to live in a hopeful present.

cues.zh: 更典型的是，我们居住的环境往往像这样。
cues.en: The environments we are living in, more typically, are like these.

cues.zh: 你知道，这恰好是我所在城镇以北两英里的建筑垃圾小行星带。
cues.en: You know, this happens to be the asteroid belt of architectural garbage two miles north of my town.

cues.zh: 记住，要创造一个有个性和品质的地方，
cues.en: And remember, to create a place of character and quality,

cues.zh: 你必须能够界定空间。
cues.en: you have to be able to define space.

cues.zh: 那么在这里是如何做到的呢？
cues.en: So how is that being accomplished here?

cues.zh: 如果你站在这边的沃尔玛停车场边缘，
cues.en: If you stand on the apron of the Wal-Mart over here

cues.zh: 试着看向那边的塔吉特商店，
cues.en: and try to look at the Target store over here,

cues.zh: 由于地球的曲率，你根本看不到它。（笑声）
cues.en: you can't see it because of the curvature of the Earth. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 这是大自然在告诉你，你界定空间的工作做得很糟糕。
cues.en: That's nature's way of telling you that you're doing a poor job of defining space.

cues.zh: 因此，这些地方将无人愿意涉足。
cues.en: Consequently, these will be places that nobody wants to be in.

cues.zh: 这些地方将不值得关心。
cues.en: These will be places that are not worth caring about.

cues.zh: 如今在美国，大约有38000个地方
cues.en: We have about, you know, 38,000 places

cues.zh: 是不值得关心的。
cues.en: that are not worth caring about in the United States today.

cues.zh: 当这样的地方多到一定程度，我们将拥有一个不值得保卫的国家。
cues.en: When we have enough of them, we're going to have a nation that's not worth defending.

cues.zh: 我希望你们在思考
cues.en: And I want you to think about that when you think about

cues.zh: 那些远在伊拉克等地的年轻男女时，能想到这一点，
cues.en: those young men and women who are over in places like Iraq,

cues.zh: 他们在沙地上洒下鲜血，
cues.en: spilling their blood in the sand,

cues.zh: 并问问自己：“他们对家乡的最后一丝念想是什么？”
cues.en: and ask yourself, "What is their last thought of home?"

cues.zh: 我希望那不是Chuck E. Cheese和Target商店之间的路缘坡道，
cues.en: I hope it's not the curb cut between the Chuck E. Cheese and the Target store

cues.zh: 因为那不足以让美国人为之流血。（掌声）
cues.en: because that's not good enough for Americans to be spilling their blood for. (Applause)

cues.zh: 我们需要这个国家有更好的地方。
cues.en: We need better places in this country.

cues.zh: 公共空间。这是一个很好的公共空间。
cues.en: Public space. This is a good public space.

cues.zh: 这是一个值得关心的地方。它定义明确。
cues.en: It's a place worth caring about. It's well defined.

cues.zh: 它显然是一个户外公共房间。
cues.en: It is emphatically an outdoor public room.

cues.zh: 它有一些非常重要的东西——
cues.en: It has something that is terribly important --

cues.zh: 它的边缘有一种所谓的活跃且可渗透的膜。
cues.en: it has what's called an active and permeable membrane around the edge.

cues.zh: 这是一种花哨的说法，意思是它有商店、酒吧、小餐馆、目的地——
cues.en: That's a fancy way of saying it's got shops, bars, bistros, destinations --

cues.zh: 东西进进出出。它是可渗透的。
cues.en: things go in and out of it. It's permeable.

cues.zh: 啤酒进进出出，女服务员进进出出，
cues.en: The beer goes in and out, the waitresses go in and out,

cues.zh: 这激活了这个地方的中心，使它成为人们想闲逛的地方。
cues.en: and that activates the center of this place and makes it a place that people want to hang out in.

cues.zh: 你知道，在其他文化的这些地方，
cues.en: You know, in these places in other cultures,

cues.zh: 人们只是因为喜欢它们而自愿去那里。
cues.en: people just go there voluntarily because they like them.

cues.zh: 我们不必在这里举办手工艺品集市来吸引人们来这里。（笑声）
cues.en: We don't have to have a craft fair here to get people to come here. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 你知道，你不必举办宽扎节。
cues.en: You know, you don't have to have a Kwanzaa festival.

cues.zh: 人们去那里只是因为待着舒服。
cues.en: People just go because it's pleasurable to be there.

cues.zh: 但在美国，我们就是这么做的。
cues.en: But this is how we do it in the United States.

cues.zh: 这可能是美国最重大的公共空间败笔，
cues.en: Probably the most significant public space failure in America,

cues.zh: 由当时的顶尖建筑师 Harry Cobb 和贝聿铭设计：
cues.en: designed by the leading architects of the day, Harry Cobb and I.M. Pei:

cues.zh: 波士顿市政厅广场。
cues.en: Boston City Hall Plaza.

cues.zh: 一个凄凉到连酒鬼都不愿去的地方。（笑声）
cues.en: A public place so dismal that the winos don't even want to go there. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 而且我们没法改，因为贝聿铭还健在，
cues.en: And we can't fix it because I.M. Pei's still alive,

cues.zh: 每年哈佛和麻省理工都会成立联合委员会来修缮它。
cues.en: and every year Harvard and M.I.T. have a joint committee to repair it.

cues.zh: 但每年都修不成，因为他们不想伤害贝聿铭的感情。
cues.en: And every year they fail to because they don't want to hurt I.M. Pei's feelings.

cues.zh: 这是大楼的另一侧。
cues.en: This is the other side of the building.

cues.zh: 这里我想是1966年左右一个国际设计奖的获奖作品。
cues.en: This was the winner of an international design award in, I think, 1966, something like that.

cues.zh: 不是贝聿铭和 Cobb 设计的，是另一家公司，
cues.en: It wasn't Pei and Cobb, another firm designed this,

cues.zh: 但全世界再多的百忧解，也没法让人对走过这个街区感到心安。
cues.en: but there's not enough Prozac in the world to make people feel OK about going down this block.

cues.zh: 这是波士顿市政厅的背面，
cues.en: This is the back of Boston City Hall,

cues.zh: 这是奥尔巴尼——抱歉——是波士顿最重要的、意义重大的市政建筑。
cues.en: the most important, you know, significant civic building in Albany -- excuse me -- in Boston.

cues.zh: 那么它传达的信息是什么，
cues.en: And what is the message that is coming,

cues.zh: 从这座建筑中传递出怎样的词汇和语法，
cues.en: what are the vocabularies and grammars that are coming, from this building

cues.zh: 它又如何让我们认识自己是谁？
cues.en: and how is it informing us about who we are?

cues.zh: 实际上，如果我们在建筑侧面放上马赛克肖像，
cues.en: This, in fact, would be a better building if we put mosaic portraits

cues.zh: 约瑟夫·斯大林、波尔布特、萨达姆·侯赛因，
cues.en: of Josef Stalin, Pol Pot, Saddam Hussein,

cues.zh: 以及20世纪所有其他大独裁者的肖像，这栋建筑反而会更好，
cues.en: and all the other great despots of the 20th century on the side of the building,

cues.zh: 因为那样我们就能诚实地表达这栋建筑真正在向我们传达什么。
cues.en: because then we'd honestly be saying what the building is really communicating to us.

cues.zh: 你知道，它是一栋专制的建筑；
cues.en: You know, that it's a despotic building;

cues.zh: 它想让我们感觉自己像白蚁。（笑声）
cues.en: it wants us to feel like termites. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 这是缩小版：
cues.en: This is it on a smaller scale:

cues.zh: 我所在城镇纽约州萨拉托加斯普林斯市民中心的背面。
cues.en: the back of the civic center in my town, Saratoga Springs, New York.

cues.zh: 顺便说一下，当我把这张幻灯片放给我镇上扶轮社的一群人看时，
cues.en: By the way, when I showed this slide to a group of Kiwanians in my town,

cues.zh: 他们都从奶油鸡肉前愤然起身，（笑声）
cues.en: they all rose in indignation from their creamed chicken, (Laughter)

cues.zh: 冲我喊叫道：
cues.en: and they shouted at me and said,

cues.zh: “你拍那张照片那天明明在下雨！”
cues.en: "It was raining that day when you took that picture!"

cues.zh: 因为大家把这当成天气问题了。（笑声）
cues.en: Because this was perceived to be a weather problem. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 你知道吗，这栋楼设计得像台DVD播放机。（笑声）
cues.en: You know, this is a building designed like a DVD player. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 音频插孔、电源接口——
cues.en: Audio jack, power supply --

cues.zh: 你看，这些对建筑事务所来说可都是重要的正经项目，对吧？
cues.en: and look, you know these things are important architectural jobs for firms, right?

cues.zh: 我们雇事务所来设计这些东西。
cues.en: You know, we hire firms to design these things.

cues.zh: 你完全能想象出发生了什么，设计会议凌晨三点钟的场景。
cues.en: You can see exactly what went on, three o'clock in the morning at the design meeting.

cues.zh: 你知道，离截止时间还有八小时，
cues.en: You know, eight hours before deadline,

cues.zh: 四个建筑师正赶着让这栋楼按时完工，对吧？
cues.en: four architects trying to get this building in on time, right?

cues.zh: 他们坐在长长的会议桌旁，
cues.en: And they're sitting there at the long boardroom table

cues.zh: 桌上摊满了图纸和效果图，
cues.en: with all the drawings, and the renderings,

cues.zh: 还有一堆中餐外卖盒躺在桌上，还有——
cues.en: and all the Chinese food caskets are lying on the table, and --

cues.zh: 我是说，当时那场对话到底在聊什么？（笑声）
cues.en: I mean, what was the conversation that was going on there? (Laughter)

cues.zh: 因为你知道那场会议最后说的话、最后一句话是什么。
cues.en: Because you know what the last word was, what the last sentence was of that meeting.

cues.zh: 原话是：“去他妈的。”（笑声）（掌声）
cues.en: It was: "Fuck it." (Laughter) (Applause)

cues.zh: 那——那就是这种建筑形式传达的信息。
cues.en: That -- that is the message of this form of architecture.

cues.zh: 信息就是：我们他妈的根本不在乎！我们他妈的根本不在乎。
cues.en: The message is: We don't give a fuck! We don't give a fuck.

cues.zh: 所以我在一年中天气最好的一天回去了，只是为了——
cues.en: So I went back on the nicest day of the year, just to --

cues.zh: 你知道——做点现实检验，
cues.en: you know -- do some reality testing,

cues.zh: 而事实上，他根本不愿去那里，因为（笑声）
cues.en: and in fact, he will not even go down there because (Laughter)

cues.zh: 那地方对他的客户来说不够有意思，
cues.en: it's not interesting enough for his clients,

cues.zh: 你知道，那些入室盗窃的、抢劫的。
cues.en: you know, the burglars, the muggers.

cues.zh: 那地方对他们来说不够有城市活力。
cues.en: It's not civically rich enough for them to go down there.

cues.zh: 好。
cues.en: OK.

cues.zh: 美国主街的模式——
cues.en: The pattern of Main Street USA --

cues.zh: 事实上，这种在全世界建造市中心街区的模式，相当普遍。
cues.en: in fact, this pattern of building downtown blocks, all over the world, is fairly universal.

cues.zh: 没那么复杂：
cues.en: It's not that complicated:

cues.zh: 建筑超过一层高，一直建到人行道边缘，
cues.en: buildings more than one story high, built out to the sidewalk edge,

cues.zh: 这样人们，你知道，各种各样的人都能进入建筑。
cues.en: so that people who are, you know, all kinds of people can get into the building.

cues.zh: 楼上可以做其他活动，
cues.en: Other activities are allowed to occur upstairs,

cues.zh: 比如公寓、办公室等等。
cues.en: you know, apartments, offices, and so on.

cues.zh: 你在底层为购物这种活动留出空间。
cues.en: You make provision for this activity called shopping on the ground floor.

cues.zh: 他们在蒙特雷没学过这个。
cues.en: They haven't learned that in Monterey.

cues.zh: 如果你走到会议中心正前方主路口那个街角，
cues.en: If you go out to the corner right at the main intersection right in front of this conference center,

cues.zh: 你会看到一个十字路口，每个角上都是光秃秃的墙。
cues.en: you'll see an intersection with four blank walls on every corner.

cues.zh: 真是难以置信。
cues.en: It's really incredible.

cues.zh: 总之，这就是你如何组合和拼装一栋市中心商业建筑，
cues.en: Anyway, this is how you compose and assemble a downtown business building,

cues.zh: 而这就是在纽约州格伦斯福尔斯发生的事，
cues.en: and this is what happened when in Glens Falls, New York,

cues.zh: 当我们想再来一次的时候——那里缺的就是这个，对吧？
cues.en: when we tried to do it again, where it was missing, right?

cues.zh: 所以他们做的第一件事，就是把零售层抬高半层，显得运动感十足。
cues.en: So the first thing they do is they pop up the retail a half a story above grade to make it sporty.

cues.zh: 好吧。这完全破坏了商铺和人行道之间的关系，
cues.en: OK. That completely destroys the relationship between the business and the sidewalk,

cues.zh: 而理论上行人就在那里。（笑声）
cues.en: where the theoretical pedestrians are. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 当然，只要这里还是这个样子，他们就永远不会去那儿。
cues.en: Of course, they'll never be there, as long as this is in that condition.

cues.zh: 因为这样一来，零售业之间的关系就被破坏了，
cues.en: Then because the relationship between the retail is destroyed,

cues.zh: 我们就在上面加一个无障碍坡道，
cues.en: we pop a handicapped ramp on that,

cues.zh: 然后为了让自己好受点，我们在前面贴个自然创可贴。
cues.en: and then to make ourselves feel better, we put a nature Band-Aid in front of it.

cues.zh: 我们就是这么干的。
cues.en: And that's how we do it.

cues.zh: 我管它们叫“自然创可贴”，因为在美国有一种普遍观念，
cues.en: I call them "nature Band-Aids" because there's a general idea in America

cues.zh: 认为被破坏的城市景观，解药就是自然。
cues.en: that the remedy for mutilated urbanism is nature.

cues.zh: 而事实上，受伤和被破坏的城市景观，解药是好的城市设计、好的建筑。
cues.en: And in fact, the remedy for wounded and mutilated urbanism is good urbanism, good buildings.

cues.zh: 不只是花坛，不只是内华达山脉的卡通画。
cues.en: Not just flower beds, not just cartoons of the Sierra Nevada Mountains.

cues.zh: 你知道，那还不够好。
cues.en: You know, that's not good enough.

cues.zh: 我们得做出好的建筑。
cues.en: We have to do good buildings.

cues.zh: 行道树其实就四个任务，仅此而已：
cues.en: The street trees have really four jobs to do and that's it:

cues.zh: 在空间上标示出人行区域，
cues.en: To spatially denote the pedestrian realm,

cues.zh: 保护行人免受车行道上的车辆伤害，
cues.en: to protect the pedestrians from the vehicles in the carriageway,

cues.zh: 把阳光过滤到人行道上，
cues.en: to filter the sunlight onto the sidewalk,

cues.zh: 柔化建筑的硬质景观，
cues.en: and to soften the hardscape of the buildings

cues.zh: 最好还能在街道上方形成一个顶棚——一个拱形顶棚。
cues.en: and to create a ceiling -- a vaulted ceiling -- over the street, at its best.

cues.zh: 就是这样。这就是行道树的四个作用。
cues.en: And that's it. Those are the four jobs of the street trees.

cues.zh: 它们不该是北方森林的卡通画；
cues.en: They're not supposed to be a cartoon of the North Woods;

cues.zh: 也不该是《最后的莫希干人》的布景。
cues.en: they're not supposed to be a set for "The Last of the Mohicans."

cues.zh: 你知道，郊区灾难的一个问题是，它破坏了我们的理解，
cues.en: You know, one of the problems with the fiasco of suburbia is that it destroyed our understanding

cues.zh: 即乡村与城镇、城市与乡野之间的区别。
cues.en: of the distinction between the country and the town, between the urban and the rural.

cues.zh: 它们不是一回事。
cues.en: They're not the same thing.

cues.zh: 我们不能靠把乡村拖进城市来解决城市的问题，
cues.en: And we're not going to cure the problems of the urban by dragging the country into the city,

cues.zh: 而这正是我们许多人一直想做的。
cues.en: which is what a lot of us are trying to do all the time.

cues.zh: 在这里你可以看到小规模的版本——母舰已经降落，
cues.en: Here you see it on a small scale -- the mothership has landed,

cues.zh: R2-D2 和 C-3PO 走出来测试树皮覆盖物，
cues.en: R2-D2 and C-3PO have stepped out to test the bark mulch

cues.zh: 看看他们能否在这个星球上居住。（笑声）
cues.en: to see if they can inhabit this planet. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 这很大程度上源于美国工业城市曾带来如此大的创伤，
cues.en: A lot of this comes from the fact that the industrial city in America was such a trauma

cues.zh: 以至于我们对城市的整个概念、
cues.en: that we developed this tremendous aversion for the whole idea of the city,

cues.zh: 城市生活以及与之相关的一切都产生了极大的厌恶。
cues.en: city life, and everything connected with it.

cues.zh: 于是，在19世纪中叶，你很快就能看到这样一种观念，
cues.en: And so what you see fairly early, in the mid-19th century,

cues.zh: 就是我们现在必须找到工业城市的解药，
cues.en: is this idea that we now have to have an antidote to the industrial city,

cues.zh: 那就是让每个人都过上乡村生活。
cues.en: which is going to be life in the country for everybody.

cues.zh: 而这一理念开始以铁路郊区的形式实现：
cues.en: And that starts to be delivered in the form of the railroad suburb:

cues.zh: 沿着铁路线分布的乡村别墅，
cues.en: the country villa along the railroad line,

cues.zh: 让人们既能享受城市的便利设施，
cues.en: which allows people to enjoy the amenity of the city,

cues.zh: 又能在每晚回归乡野。
cues.en: but to return to the countryside every night.

cues.zh: 相信我，那时候那里可没有沃尔玛或便利店，
cues.en: And believe me, there were no Wal-Marts or convenience stores out there then,

cues.zh: 所以那确实算得上是一种乡村生活。
cues.en: so it really was a form of country living.

cues.zh: 但接下来发生的是，在随后的80年里，它发生了变异，
cues.en: But what happens is, of course, it mutates over the next 80 years

cues.zh: 变成了一种相当隐蔽的东西。
cues.en: and it turns into something rather insidious.

cues.zh: 它变成了一幅乡村别墅的漫画，置身于一幅乡村的漫画之中。
cues.en: It becomes a cartoon of a country house, in a cartoon of the country.

cues.zh: 这就是郊区生活那种巨大的、难以言说的痛苦，
cues.en: And that's the great non-articulated agony of suburbia

cues.zh: 也是它容易沦为笑柄的原因之一。
cues.en: and one of the reasons that it lends itself to ridicule.

cues.zh: 因为它至今没能兑现半个世纪以来的承诺。
cues.en: Because it hasn't delivered what it's been promising for half a century now.

cues.zh: 这些就是我们通常在那里看到的住宅类型。
cues.en: And these are typically the kind of dwellings we find there, you know.

cues.zh: 基本上，就是一栋侧面什么都没有的房子
cues.en: Basically, a house with nothing on the side

cues.zh: 因为这栋房子想强调地表明，
cues.en: because this house wants to state, emphatically,

cues.zh: “我是树林里的一间小木屋。我两边什么都没有。
cues.en: "I'm a little cabin in the woods. There's nothing on either side of me.

cues.zh: 我脑袋侧面没有眼睛。我看不见。”
cues.en: I don't have any eyes on the side of my head. I can't see."

cues.zh: 所以你就有了房子最后一面立面，
cues.en: So you have this one last facade of the house,

cues.zh: 正面，那其实是一幅房子立面的漫画。
cues.en: the front, which is really a cartoon of a facade of a house.

cues.zh: 因为——注意这里的门廊。
cues.en: Because -- notice the porch here.

cues.zh: 除非住在这里的人是芒奇金人，否则没人会用得上那个。
cues.en: Unless the people that live here are Munchkins, nobody's going to be using that.

cues.zh: 这实际上是一台电视机，24小时不间断播放一档叫“我们很正常”的节目。
cues.en: This is really, in fact, a television broadcasting a show 24/7 called "We're Normal."

cues.zh: 我们很正常，我们很正常，我们很正常，我们很正常，我们很正常。
cues.en: We're normal, we're normal, we're normal, we're normal, we're normal.

cues.zh: 请尊重我们，我们很正常，我们很正常，我们很正常。
cues.en: Please respect us, we're normal, we're normal, we're normal.

cues.zh: 但我们知道这些房子里在发生什么，你知道的。
cues.en: But we know what's going on in these houses, you know.

cues.zh: 我们知道小斯基皮在下面装填他的乌兹冲锋枪，
cues.en: We know that little Skippy is loading his Uzi down here,

cues.zh: 准备去上课。（笑声）
cues.en: getting ready for homeroom. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 我们知道他的姐姐希瑟，14岁，
cues.en: We know that Heather, his sister Heather, 14 years old,

cues.zh: 在上面卖身来支撑她的毒瘾。
cues.en: is turning tricks up here to support her drug habit.

cues.zh: 因为这些地方，这些居住环境，
cues.en: Because these places, these habitats,

cues.zh: 正在给孩子们带来大量的焦虑和抑郁，
cues.en: are inducing immense amounts of anxiety and depression in children,

cues.zh: 而他们对药物治疗没什么经验。
cues.en: and they don't have a lot of experience with medication.

cues.zh: 所以他们往往就吃第一种到手的药。
cues.en: So they take the first one that comes along, often.

cues.zh: 这些对美国人来说还不够好。
cues.en: These are not good enough for Americans.

cues.zh: 这些就是我们送他们去的学校：
cues.en: These are the schools we are sending them to:

cues.zh: 内华达州拉斯维加斯的汉尼拔·莱克特中央学校。
cues.en: The Hannibal Lecter Central School, Las Vegas, Nevada.

cues.zh: 这是一所真实的学校！
cues.en: This is a real school!

cues.zh: 你知道，但显然有一种观念认为，如果你把这里的囚犯放出去，
cues.en: You know, but there's obviously a notion that if you let the inmates of this thing out,

cues.zh: 他们就会从街上抓个司机，吃掉他的肝脏。
cues.en: that they would snatch a motorist off the street and eat his liver.

cues.zh: 所以人们竭尽全力把它们留在楼里。
cues.en: So every effort is made to keep them within the building.

cues.zh: 注意，大自然就在那里。（笑声）
cues.en: Notice that nature is present. (Laughter)

cues.zh: 不管我们愿不愿意，我们都必须改变这种行为。
cues.en: We're going to have to change this behavior whether we like it or not.

cues.zh: 我们正在进入世界上一个划时代的变革时期，而且——尤其是在美国
cues.en: We are entering an epochal period of change in the world, and -- certainly in America

cues.zh: ——这个时期将以廉价石油时代的终结为特征。
cues.en: -- the period that will be characterized by the end of the cheap oil era.

cues.zh: 它将彻底改变一切。
cues.en: It is going to change absolutely everything.

cues.zh: Chris让我不要在这个问题上讲太久，我不会的，
cues.en: Chris asked me not to go on too long about this, and I won't,

cues.zh: 只是要说，不会出现氢经济。
cues.en: except to say there's not going to be a hydrogen economy.

cues.zh: 算了吧。那不会发生的。
cues.en: Forget it. It's not going to happen.

cues.zh: 我们得另想办法。
cues.en: We're going to have to do something else instead.

cues.zh: 我们将不得不缩减规模、重新调整规模、重新设定大小，
cues.en: We're going to have to down-scale, re-scale, and re-size

cues.zh: 几乎涉及我们在这个国家所做的每一件事，而且我们开始得再快也不为过。
cues.en: virtually everything we do in this country and we can't start soon enough to do it.

cues.zh: 我们将会——（掌声）——我们将会不得不住在离工作地点更近的地方。
cues.en: We're going to have -- (Applause) -- we're going to have to live closer to where we work.

cues.zh: 我们将会不得不住得彼此更近。
cues.en: We're going to have to live closer to each other.

cues.zh: 我们将会不得不在离居住地更近的地方种植更多食物。
cues.en: We're going have to grow more food closer to where we live.

cues.zh: 三千英里凯撒沙拉的时代即将终结。
cues.en: The age of the 3,000 mile Caesar salad is coming to an end.

cues.zh: 我们将会不得不——我们的铁路系统，连保加利亚人都会为之羞愧！
cues.en: We're going to have to -- we have a railroad system that the Bulgarians would be ashamed of!

cues.zh: 我们必须做得比那更好！
cues.en: We gotta do better than that!

cues.zh: 而且我们本该在前天之前就开始行动。
cues.en: And we should have started two days before yesterday.

cues.zh: 我们很幸运，过去十年里有新城市主义者在那里，
cues.en: We are fortunate that the new urbanists were there, for the last 10 years,

cues.zh: 挖掘出所有那些被扔进垃圾堆的信息
cues.en: excavating all that information that was thrown in the garbage

cues.zh: 被我们父母那一代在二战后丢弃的。
cues.en: by our parents' generation after World War II.

cues.zh: 因为如果我们要学习如何重建城镇，就会需要这些。
cues.en: Because we're going to need it if we're going to learn how to reconstruct towns.

cues.zh: 我们需要找回这一整套方法论、原则和技能
cues.en: We're going to need to get back this body of methodology and principle and skill

cues.zh: 以便重新学习如何构建有意义的地方，那些完整一体的地方，
cues.en: in order to re-learn how to compose meaningful places, places that are integral,

cues.zh: 那些允许——那些是活的有机体，因为它们包含了我们公民生活
cues.en: that allow -- that are living organisms in the sense that they contain all the organs of our civic life

cues.zh: 和社区生活的所有器官，以完整一体化的方式部署。
cues.en: and our communal life, deployed in an integral fashion.

cues.zh: 这样一来，住宅区就合理了
cues.en: So that, you know, the residences make sense

cues.zh: 它们与商业、文化及治理场所的布局息息相关。
cues.en: deployed in relation to the places of business, of culture and of governance.

cues.zh: 我们得重新认识这些事物的基本构成单元：
cues.en: We're going to have to re-learn what the building blocks of these things are:

cues.zh: 街道、街区，如何构建大小兼备的公共空间，
cues.en: the street, the block, how to compose public space that's both large and small,

cues.zh: 庭院、市民广场
cues.en: the courtyard, the civic square

cues.zh: 以及如何真正利用好这片土地。
cues.en: and how to really make use of this property.

cues.zh: 我们可以看到一些初步构想
cues.en: We can see some of the first ideas

cues.zh: 针对美国那些灾难性地产的改造方案。
cues.en: for retro-fitting some of the catastrophic property that we have in America.

cues.zh: 那些废弃的商场：我们该如何处理它们？
cues.en: The dead malls: what are we going to do with them?

cues.zh: 事实上，它们中的大多数都将无法挽救。
cues.en: Well, in point of fact, most of them are not going to make it.

cues.zh: 它们不会被改造；
cues.en: They're not going to be retro-fitted;

cues.zh: 它们将成为未来的废料场。
cues.en: they're going to be the salvage yards of the future.

cues.zh: 不过，其中一些我们还是会修复的。
cues.en: Some of them we're going to fix, though.

cues.zh: 我们要通过重新引入街道和街区系统来修复它们
cues.en: And we're going to fix them by imposing back on them street and block systems

cues.zh: 并回归到以地块作为开发的常规增量单位
cues.en: and returning to the building lot as the normal increment of development.

cues.zh: 如果幸运的话，结果将是焕然一新的城镇中心和社区中心
cues.en: And if we're lucky, the result will be revivified town centers and neighborhood centers

cues.zh: 就在我们现有的城镇和城市中。
cues.en: in our existing towns and cities.

cues.zh: 顺便说一句，我们的城镇和城市就在它们所在的地方，在它们原来的地方发展起来
cues.en: And by the way, our towns and cities are where they are, and grew where they were

cues.zh: 因为它们占据了所有重要的位置。
cues.en: because they occupy all the important sites.

cues.zh: 它们中的大多数仍然会留在那里，
cues.en: And most of them are still going to be there,

cues.zh: 尽管它们的规模可能会缩小。
cues.en: although the scale of them is probably going to be diminished.

cues.zh: 我们有很多工作要做。
cues.en: We've got a lot of work to do.

cues.zh: 我们不会靠超级汽车得救；我们不会靠替代燃料得救。
cues.en: We're not going to be rescued by the hyper-car; we're not going to be rescued by alternative fuels.

cues.zh: 任何数量或组合的替代燃料
cues.en: No amount or combination of alternative fuels

cues.zh: 都无法让我们继续以现在的方式运转我们所运转的一切。
cues.en: is going to allow us to continue running what we're running, the way we're running it.

cues.zh: 我们得彻底改变做事方式。
cues.en: We're going to have to do everything very differently.

cues.zh: 而美国还没准备好。
cues.en: And America's not prepared.

cues.zh: 我们正梦游般走向未来。
cues.en: We are sleepwalking into the future.

cues.zh: 我们对即将到来的一切毫无准备。
cues.en: We're not ready for what's coming at us.

cues.zh: 所以我恳请大家尽力而为。
cues.en: So I urge you all to do what you can.

cues.zh: 21世纪中叶的生活将围绕本地化展开。
cues.en: Life in the mid-21st century is going to be about living locally.

cues.zh: 准备好做个好邻居。
cues.en: Be prepared to be good neighbors.

cues.zh: 准备好找到能让你发挥作用的职业
cues.en: Be prepared to find vocations that make you useful

cues.zh: 为邻里和同胞服务。
cues.en: to your neighbors and to your fellow citizens.

cues.zh: 最后一件事——多年来我一直为此深感不安，
cues.en: One final thing -- I've been very disturbed about this for years,

cues.zh: 但我认为对在座各位尤为重要。
cues.en: but I think it's particularly important for this audience.

cues.zh: 请你们，请你们别再自称“消费者”了，好吗？
cues.en: Please, please, stop referring to yourselves as "consumers." OK?

cues.zh: 消费者和公民是不同的。
cues.en: Consumers are different than citizens.

cues.zh: 消费者没有义务、责任和职责
cues.en: Consumers do not have obligations, responsibilities and duties

cues.zh: 去对待自己的同胞。
cues.en: to their fellow human beings.

cues.zh: 只要你在公开讨论中使用“消费者”这个词，
cues.en: And as long as you're using that word consumer in the public discussion,

cues.zh: 就会降低我们讨论的质量。
cues.en: you will be degrading the quality of the discussion we're having.

cues.zh: 而我们将继续一无所知，
cues.en: And we're going to continue being clueless

cues.zh: 走进我们面临的这个非常艰难的未来。
cues.en: going into this very difficult future that we face.

cues.zh: 非常感谢。
cues.en: So thank you very much.

cues.zh: 请大家行动起来，尽你所能，让这片土地充满值得关心的地方，
cues.en: Please go out and do what you can to make this a land full of places that are worth caring about

cues.zh: 成为一个值得捍卫的国家。（掌声）
cues.en: and a nation that will be worth defending. (Applause)
